items.title: Frank Chace Interview, 1961-11-18
items.q: I, I only know the records, naturally.

ctx.x: Well, Jacobson told me once that he felt a little resentment of Teschmacher because he felt Teschmacher was a little overbearing in his playing. He kind of took over the band. He, I don't know, I don't know if he had particular volume, but he, but that crashing attack that he'd play with evidently riled some of the other members in the orchestras he was working with. They thought he was, he was fighting too hard, he was playing a little too desperately. But for my part, that's what I love. I, I only know the…

Do you think it might have been, uh, just that he hadn't been playing long enough to command the instrument, that is five more years, and Teschmacher might have played with a clean execution, yet using the same, uh, uh, fierce dynamics? Maybe it's possible to play that way.
